Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres hosting platform, production). Work ONLY in an isolated git worktree — `git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-namecheap -b feature/namecheap-registrar` from /opt/nxeon — do NOT touch the live /opt/nxeon tree or merge into main. Symlink node_modules and .env from /opt/nxeon; never `git add -A` in a worktree (a documented past incident replaced prod's real node_modules with a self-referential symlink).

## Context — read this plan file first

A full multi-registrar plan already exists and was partially executed: `/root/.claude/plans/validated-napping-possum.md` — read it in full before starting. Phase 1 (consolidating 3 duplicate name.com HTTP clients into `lib/registrar.ts`) is DONE and live. Phase 5 (closing customer-facing registrar-identity leaks — never naming "name.com"/"Namecheap"/"eNom" to a signed-in customer, admin-only visibility) is ALSO DONE and live — read `test/registrar-leak-guard.test.ts` to understand the enforced invariant, since anything you add must not violate it. Phase 2 (the actual `RegistrarClient` abstraction + a second registrar) was deliberately DEFERRED pending real credentials — those now exist, this is that work.

**Scope change from the plan document**: eNom is OFF THE TABLE — they do not offer an API. This is Namecheap-only for the second registrar. Skip anything in the plan document that was eNom-specific.

## Credentials now available

`.env` (already populated, read it): `NAMECHEAP_API_KEY` (real, live key), `NAMECHEAP_CLIENT_IP=51.79.162.96` (Nxeon's real outbound IP, already correct). **`NAMECHEAP_API_USER` and `NAMECHEAP_USERNAME` are still BLANK** — Namecheap's API requires ApiUser + ApiKey + UserName + ClientIp on every call (ApiUser and UserName are typically identical — the account's login username). You cannot make a real authenticated call without these. Build everything correctly against them being env-driven, verify your code compiles and the request-shape is right, but do not expect a real API call to succeed yet — that's expected and fine, note it clearly in your report rather than treating it as a bug in your code.

**Also critical**: Namecheap's API only accepts requests from IPs explicitly whitelisted in the account's own dashboard (Profile → Tools → Business & Dev Tools → API Access → Whitelisted IPs) — there is no API endpoint to do this remotely, it's a manual step only the account owner can do in Namecheap's web UI. `51.79.162.96` (already in `.env`) is the IP that needs whitelisting. State this plainly and prominently in your report as an owner action item, since even with full credentials, every real API call will fail with an IP-not-whitelisted error until this is done manually.

## What to build

1. **`lib/registrars/types.ts`** — the `RegistrarClient` interface, per the plan document's Phase 2 section: `checkDomains`, `registerDomain`, `renewDomain`, `domainInfo`, `disableRegistrarAutorenew`, the inbound-transfer lifecycle (`checkTransfer`/`createTransfer`/`getTransfer`/`cancelTransfer`/`listTransfers`), DNS CRUD (`listRecords`/`addRecord`/`deleteRecord`/`getDnsHosts`), nameserver/WHOIS/lock/forwarding functions (already consolidated for name.com in `lib/registrar.ts` from Phase 1 — read that file fully to match its exact function signatures so both registrars satisfy the same interface shape). Each implementation exposes `id` ("namecom"/"namecheap") and `label` ("name.com"/"Namecheap") — `label` is ADMIN-DISPLAY-ONLY, per the leak-guard test, never passed to a customer-facing function or string.

2. **`lib/registrars/namecheap.ts`** — the real Namecheap client. Namecheap's API is XML-based via query-string GET requests (`namecheap.domains.check`, `.create`, `.renew`, `.dns.setHosts`, `.transfer.create`, etc.) — this repo already depends on `fast-xml-parser` (confirm in package.json), use it to parse responses. Auth params (`ApiUser`, `ApiKey`, `UserName`, `ClientIp`) go on every request per Namecheap's documented shape — WebFetch/WebSearch Namecheap's current official API documentation (developer.namecheap.com) to get the exact parameter names, endpoint paths, and response XML structure right — do not guess from memory, this is exactly the kind of external API detail that's easy to get subtly wrong. Verify sandbox vs. production base URL handling (`api.sandbox.namecheap.com` vs `api.namecheap.com`) and gate it the same defensive way `lib/paypal.ts` gates Stripe/PayPal mode (default to the SAFER option when ambiguous, never silently default to live).

3. **`lib/registrars/index.ts`** — `ALL_REGISTRARS`, `configuredRegistrars()` (checks env-var presence AND an admin-toggleable setting — follow `lib/settings.ts`'s existing kill-switch pattern, e.g. `registrar_namecheap_enabled` defaulting to `"false"` until the owner has verified it end-to-end), `registrarById(id)`.

4. **Price-shopping / fan-out**: read `lib/tools/domain-availability.ts` (the shared cache/batch/rate-limit wrapper). Extend it to fan out across `configuredRegistrars()` — each registrar keeps its own cache key (`(registrarId, domain)`), own batch size (verify Namecheap's real batching limit from their docs, don't assume it matches name.com's), own rate-limit bucket. Merge: cheapest `available: true` wins; "taken" only if at least one registrar explicitly says so; "unknown" if every registrar is unknown — never fabricate a status.

5. **Renewal price display — the second major deliverable**: domains very often renew at a HIGHER price than the first-year registration price (a real, common registrar practice), and this platform currently does not clearly surface that distinction anywhere a customer would see it before buying (verify this claim by checking the domain search UI, cart/checkout, and order confirmation — `components/customer/DomainSearch.tsx`, `components/customer/DomainRegisterWizard.tsx`, `app/dashboard/domains/**`). Namecheap's `domains.check` / pricing API returns both registration AND renewal price per TLD — capture and surface both. Check what name.com's existing integration (`lib/registrar.ts`) already returns — it likely already has renewal pricing available even if the UI never displays it (check its response types before assuming you need to add a new field). Add clear "renews at $X/yr" copy wherever a domain's first-year price is shown, for BOTH registrars, so a customer never discovers a renewal price surprise after the fact. This is a real, valuable trust/deliverability feature independent of whether Namecheap ever goes fully live — if name.com already has the data, ship the display for name.com now too, don't gate it behind Namecheap being ready.

6. **Schema**: if the current `Domain`/pricing models don't already have a field for the frozen renewal price shown at purchase time, add one (mirroring how `DomainOrderPrice`/`DomainOrderIntent` already freeze `priceCents`/`costCents` at quote time per the plan document's Finding 2 — a renewal price should be frozen the same way, not re-fetched live at renewal time, so what was SHOWN is what's CHARGED).

## What NOT to do

- Do not touch the custom-server-plans feature, PayPal, or the Nxeon board — separate agents, separate worktrees, working in parallel right now.
- Do not violate the leak-guard test — re-run `npm test -- test/registrar-leak-guard.test.ts` style check (or just the full suite) before finishing; if you add any new customer-facing domain UI copy, scan it yourself against the same forbidden-pattern logic first.
- Do not enable `registrar_namecheap_enabled` by default — ship it OFF, per the plan document's staged-rollout philosophy (Phase 7): a brand-new registrar integration with credentials that can't even authenticate yet (missing ApiUser/UserName, IP not whitelisted) must not be live by default.

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. `npm test` — no new failures beyond the 34 pre-existing baseline (ask if you need the exact list; it's dominated by pricing/proration/auth-baseline tests unrelated to registrars — the EXISTING `test/registrar-leak-guard.test.ts` and `test/registrar-error.test.ts` must still pass unchanged).
3. Add tests for: the merge-cheapest logic across two registrars (agreement, disagreement, all-unknown), the renewal-price-frozen-at-quote-time behavior, and Namecheap's XML response parsing (use a realistic sample response body, don't just test against your own mocked shape).

## Report format

1. Exact Namecheap API endpoints/params used, with a link/citation to where you verified them.
2. Confirmation of what's still needed before this can go live: `NAMECHEAP_API_USER`/`NAMECHEAP_USERNAME` values from the owner, AND the IP-whitelisting step in Namecheap's dashboard — both stated plainly.
3. What you found for name.com's existing renewal-price data (did it already exist and just need surfacing, or did you have to add it there too).
4. Files created/modified, verification results, worktree path/branch name.

# Multi-registrar domain sourcing (name.com + Namecheap + Enom)

## Context

Nxeon sells domains through exactly one registrar today (name.com), via a reseller API. The owner wants to add Namecheap and Enom as additional backends so that every domain search/purchase automatically uses whichever registrar is cheapest after Nxeon's markup — maximizing margin and/or offering customers the best price — while the registrar's identity stays completely invisible to customers (search results, error messages, DNS/nameserver copy, the AI chat assistant) and visible only in admin views, per-domain.

This scope was built from a full audit of the existing registrar code and every customer-facing surface that currently names "name.com" directly. Two structural findings shape the whole plan:

- **There are 3 separate hardcoded name.com HTTP clients today**, not one: `lib/registrar.ts` (the main one), plus private duplicates inside `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` (nameservers/WHOIS/outbound-transfer) and `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` (URL forwarding/registrar lock). Designing a multi-registrar interface against 3 different existing shapes at once is how it ends up wrong in three different ways — they must be consolidated into one `NameComRegistrar` implementation FIRST, as a pure no-behavior-change refactor, before any second registrar is added.
- **The registrar decision must freeze at the same moment as the price it's paired with.** `purchaseDomain`'s direct-wallet path re-quotes fresh right before charging; its card path freezes `{priceCents, costCents}` into a `DomainOrderIntent` row at Stripe-session-creation time and never re-quotes at fulfillment. Once multiple registrars exist, "cheapest registrar" is part of that same frozen quote — `DomainOrderPrice`/`DomainOrderIntent` need a `registrar` field alongside `priceCents`/`costCents`, not a separate re-decision step later. Getting this wrong means a card order quoted against one registrar could silently try to fulfill through a different (by-then-cheaper) one, which has no record of that domain — invisible to the customer, but a real operational bug.

Also found: `Domain.registrar` (`prisma/schema.prisma`) already has `@default("namecheap")` even though every write site hardcodes the literal `"name.com"` — a landmine nobody has hit yet only because every create site sets it explicitly. Fix this default as part of the schema work.

## Confirmed customer-facing registrar-identity leaks (must be closed as part of this work)

1. `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx:83` — nameserver label literally "Default (name.com)".
2. `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:346` — a badge reading "name.com DNS".
3. `components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:80,87` — "name.com" badge + "moves DNS off name.com's servers" copy.
4. `components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx:68,72,147,219` — "live via name.com" / "name.com URL forwarding" copy (×3).
5. `lib/actions-domains.ts:344` — customer-facing error string says "(name.com API keys missing)".
6. **Biggest leak vector**: every `nc()`-style helper throws `` `name.com: ${msg}` ``, and every catch site across `lib/actions-domains*.ts` passes that raw message straight through as `{error: ...}` into customer components — so any registrar-side failure (e.g. the real "name.com: Payment failed" seen in production) is shown verbatim, registrar name included.
7. `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`'s `setWhoisPrivacy()` returns a customer-facing note interpolating `` `WHOIS privacy at ${domain.registrar}...` ``.
8. `lib/kb-tools.ts:642` — `describeService()` feeds `` `Registrar: ${domain.registrar}` `` into the AI live-chat assistant's context, which a signed-in customer's chat could echo back.

## Approach

### Phase 1 — Consolidate the 3 name.com clients into one `NameComRegistrar`

Pure refactor, zero behavior change, ships to production on its own before any second registrar exists. Move every name.com call currently duplicated in `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` (`updateNameservers`, `setWhoisPrivacy`, `requestTransferOut`'s unlock/getAuthCode) and `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` (URL forwarding CRUD, registrar lock) into `lib/registrar.ts` as new exported functions. Delete both files' private `nc()`/`baseUrl()`/`authHeader()` clones; both call sites import the consolidated exports instead. This collapses 3 separate `` `name.com: ${msg}` `` error-formatting sites down to 1, which Phase 5 depends on. Verify with `npm test` plus a full staging smoke pass (nameserver update, WHOIS toggle, transfer-out unlock, URL forwarding CRUD, registrar lock toggle) before touching anything else.

### Phase 2 — The `RegistrarClient` abstraction

New `lib/registrars/types.ts` defines the interface covering everything a registrar does today: `checkDomains`, `registerDomain`, `renewDomain`, `domainInfo`, `disableRegistrarAutorenew`, the inbound-transfer lifecycle (`checkTransfer`/`createTransfer`/`getTransfer`/`cancelTransfer`/`listTransfers`), DNS CRUD (`listRecords`/`addRecord`/`deleteRecord`/`getDnsHosts`), and the Phase-1-consolidated nameserver/WHOIS/lock/forwarding functions. Each implementation also exposes `id` ("namecom"/"namecheap"/"enom", the DB/dispatch value) and `label` ("name.com"/"Namecheap"/"eNom", admin-display-only — never passed to a customer-facing function). `transferOutcome`/`transferStatusLabel` and `domainMarkupPct`/`retailCents` stay free, registrar-agnostic functions — status bucketing and markup are platform concepts, not per-registrar behavior.

`lib/registrars/index.ts` exports `ALL_REGISTRARS`, `configuredRegistrars()` (env-configured AND admin-enabled, see Phase 7), and `registrarById(id)`.

**Dispatch rule**: for a domain that already has a DB row, every call site resolves `registrarById(domain.registrar)` and calls through that — critical because a domain fulfilled through Namecheap has no record at name.com, so it must never silently fail over to a different backend even if that backend later gets disabled for new business. For a new search/quote (no DB row yet) or a new inbound-transfer quote, fan out to `configuredRegistrars()` instead (Phase 3).

### Phase 3 — Price-shopping mechanism

`lib/tools/domain-availability.ts`'s `checkAvailabilityBatched()` (the shared cache/batch/rate-limit wrapper used by both the marketing domain checker and the signed-in wizard) becomes a fan-out: each configured registrar keeps its own cache entries (key becomes `(registrarId, domain)`, since two registrars quoting the same domain are two different facts), its own batch size (name.com's verified 24/call does not necessarily apply to Namecheap/Enom — must be verified per-registrar against real endpoints), and its own rate-limit bucket (`` `registrar:availability:${registrarId}:global` ``, so one registrar's outage/slowness can't throttle the others). Merge step: for each domain, pick the lowest `priceCents` among registrars reporting `available: true`; treat a domain as "taken" only if at least one registrar explicitly says so; if every registrar returns `unknown`, the merged result is `unknown`, never a fabricated status. The customer-facing `DomainResult` type never carries a registrar id — that only exists in an internal-only return path used by `purchaseDomain`'s pre-charge re-quote and the eventual `Domain.registrar` write, so registrar identity is kept out of the client bundle by construction, not convention.

The purchase-time re-check (`checkDomains([domain])`, currently called fresh right before charging) becomes `quoteCheapest(domain)`, fanning out to all configured registrars with no cache (this is deliberately the anti-staleness check), returning the winning `{registrar, check}`. `DomainOrderPrice`/`DomainOrderIntent` gain a `registrar` field so the card-payment path's frozen quote and the eventual `registerDomain`/`disableRegistrarAutorenew` calls agree on which backend to use.

**Markup stays a single global percentage** (`domainMarkupPct()`, unchanged) applied uniformly to whichever registrar's cost wins — this keeps "cheapest cost," "cheapest retail," and "best margin for Nxeon" all pointing at the same registrar automatically, avoiding a three-way tradeoff. Per-registrar differential markup is an explicit non-goal unless requested separately.

### Phase 4 — Real Namecheap/Enom integration work (owner action items called out plainly)

I have not verified current 2026 account-approval terms, minimum-balance requirements, or sandbox capabilities for either registrar — these change and are gated behind an application process, so they need to be checked directly against each registrar's live reseller documentation before committing to a timeline:

- **Namecheap**: historically account-age/spend-gated API access (not a separate paid tier), IP-allowlisted auth (Nxeon's production egress IP must be registered and kept in sync), XML-based responses via query-string GET commands (`namecheap.domains.check`, `.create`, `.renew`, `.dns.setHosts`, `.transfer.create`) — needs an XML parser (`fast-xml-parser` is already a dependency), unlike name.com's plain JSON REST. Has historically offered a sandbox (`api.sandbox.namecheap.com`) — confirm whether registration actually completes there or only availability checks work.
- **Enom**: Tucows-owned (same parent as name.com), historically a more traditional paid reseller program — do not assume it mirrors name.com's terms. Auth via username + API password over query-string GET; response format historically XML with a newer JSON option — confirm current default. Its test-environment story is the least documented of the three; budget real discovery time here, since its absence would mean `EnomRegistrar` can only be verified against small real production transactions.

Each new registrar gets its own `lib/registrars/namecheap.ts` / `lib/registrars/enom.ts` with its own private HTTP helper — there's no meaningful shared transport code across three structurally different APIs; the Phase-1 consolidation win is entirely about eliminating name.com's *own* triplication.

### Phase 5 — Closing the leak surface

**Static UI copy** (leaks #1–4): one constant module (e.g. `lib/registrar-copy.ts`) exporting neutral labels ("our registrar partner" / generic DNS copy — exact wording is a product call, see Open Questions), used at each of the 4 file locations instead of the literal string. Add a standing test (`test/*.test.ts`, this repo's existing pattern) that greps `components/customer/**` and `app/dashboard/**` for `"name.com"`/`"namecheap"`/`"enom"` and fails if found outside an admin allowlist — turns this from a one-time fix into an enforced invariant, which matters more with 3 registrars than 1.

**Dynamic leaks** (#5–8, the structural fix): introduce a `RegistrarError` class at the `RegistrarClient` HTTP-helper boundary carrying `{registrarId, rawMessage, customerMessage}` — `customerMessage` is a generic, pattern-matched, registrar-name-free string ("We couldn't complete this with our registrar right now — no charge was made, try again or contact support" for known failure categories, a generic fallback otherwise). The ~15 call sites across `lib/actions-domains*.ts` that currently do `{error: errMsg(e)}` read `e.customerMessage` when `e instanceof RegistrarError`, while `e.rawMessage` + `registrarId` still get logged server-side for ops. This is the single highest-leverage fix — it closes the actual production incident (raw "name.com: Payment failed" shown to a customer) at the source, for all three registrars, rather than patching call sites as they're discovered. `lib/actions-domains.ts:344`'s copy becomes registrar-neutral ("domain registration is not configured yet"); `setWhoisPrivacy`'s note drops the `${domain.registrar}` interpolation; `lib/kb-tools.ts:642` drops the `Registrar: ...` line from the AI context entirely (no product value, pure risk).

**Admin side** (where registrar identity SHOULD show): add a "Registrar" column to `app/admin/domains/page.tsx`'s table, rendering the already-populated `d.registrar` field directly — purely additive. Replace the page's single "Registrar: name.com" stat card and "via name.com" header copy with per-registrar configured/enabled status, since one value no longer describes the system.

### Phase 6 — Data migration

**None needed.** The one domain that ever completed a registration attempt was FAILED and has since been deleted — production has zero domain rows today. Just fix the schema's stray `@default("namecheap")` (drop the default entirely, or default to `"namecom"` matching current real behavior) as part of the Phase-2 schema change; no backfill script, no reclassification logic. Sanity-check with `SELECT count(*) FROM "Domain"` immediately before shipping the schema change, purely to confirm this hasn't changed.

### Phase 7 — Staged rollout

1. Ship Phase 1 (consolidation) alone, to production, first — isolates "did the refactor break name.com" from anything multi-registrar.
2. Add per-registrar admin kill-switches in `lib/settings.ts` (`registrar_namecom_enabled` default `"true"`, `registrar_namecheap_enabled`/`registrar_enom_enabled` default `"false"`), same pattern as the existing `kb_bot_enabled` flag. `configuredRegistrars()` checks both env-var presence and this setting.
3. Ship the `RegistrarClient` abstraction with Namecheap/Enom flags OFF — behaviorally identical to today, isolating "did the abstraction regress name.com" from "does a new registrar work."
4. Enable Namecheap in staging once credentials exist; run the full lifecycle (search, register, renew, DNS, nameservers, WHOIS, outbound transfer, inbound transfer quote/submit/poll/cancel) before flipping it on in production. Repeat independently for Enom — never enable both for the first time simultaneously, so a bad merge (e.g. a malformed response corrupting the cheapest-price pick) has a precise, single kill-switch to hit.
5. No new monitoring primitive needed — `registerDomainCore`'s existing `verifyRegistration`/needs-review machinery already handles ambiguous registrar failures per-domain once dispatch goes through `registrarById(domain.registrar)`; just confirm admin's needs-review/FAILED views also show the new Registrar column so ops can tell which backend is failing.
6. Land the Phase-5 leak-guard test in CI so it runs on every future PR, not just once at launch — a manual QA pass won't catch a leak introduced months later by an unrelated feature.

## Open questions for the owner (not blocking the plan, but blocking Phase 4+ timeline)

1. **Namecheap/Enom account approval, minimum balance, and sandbox capability** — needs verifying directly against each registrar's current reseller program; I can't confirm 2026 terms from here. If either lacks a real registration sandbox, staging verification for that registrar's purchase path may not be possible pre-production.
2. **Exact neutral copy** for the "our registrar partner"-style UI strings (Phase 5) — a wording preference, not a technical decision.
3. **What the customer sees, if anything, about multi-sourcing** — recommend the search results page stays byte-for-byte identical to today (say nothing about multiple providers), since the requirement is registrar identity must be invisible; confirm this is the intent versus wanting a subtle "we shop multiple providers" trust signal.
4. **Registrars disagreeing on availability** (registry sync lag) — recommend: available if any configured registrar says available with a price; taken only if none do; log disagreements for ops. This is a customer-trust/messaging call worth the owner's sign-off, not just an engineering default.

## Critical files

- `lib/registrar.ts` — becomes `NameComRegistrar`, absorbs the 2 duplicate clients (Phase 1)
- `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` — lose their private HTTP clients (Phase 1)
- `lib/registrars/types.ts`, `lib/registrars/index.ts`, `lib/registrars/namecheap.ts`, `lib/registrars/enom.ts` — new (Phase 2, 4)
- `lib/tools/domain-availability.ts` — fan-out + merge (Phase 3)
- `lib/actions-domains.ts` — `purchaseDomain`/`registerDomainCore`/`DomainOrderIntent` gain registrar dispatch (Phase 3)
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — `Domain.registrar` default fix, `DomainOrderIntent.registrar` field (Phase 2, 6)
- `app/admin/domains/page.tsx` — per-domain Registrar column + multi-registrar status cards (Phase 5)
- `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx`, `components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx`, `components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx`, `lib/kb-tools.ts` — leak fixes (Phase 5)
- `lib/settings.ts` — per-registrar kill-switches (Phase 7)

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after each phase.
2. `npm test` — zero new failures against the existing baseline, plus new tests for: the merge-cheapest logic (registrars disagreeing, all-unknown case), the `RegistrarError` customer-message mapping, and the Phase-5 leak-guard grep test.
3. Staging smoke pass per Phase 1 (consolidation) and Phase 7 step 4 (full per-registrar lifecycle) before any production flag flip.
4. Manual check: with Namecheap/Enom flags on in staging, confirm the browser network tab and rendered HTML never contain "namecheap"/"enom"/"name.com" on any customer-facing page, while `/admin/domains` correctly shows which registrar fulfilled each test domain.

/**
 * Shared source-reading helpers for the structural tripwire suites.
 *
 * NOT named `*.test.ts` on purpose: `npm test` globs `test/*.test.ts`, so this
 * module is imported, never executed as a suite. It used to live inside
 * customer-actions-guards.test.ts and be imported from there, which made every
 * assertion in that file run a second time under the importing suite's name.
 */

/**
 * Blank out the CONTENTS of every string / template literal, on top of
 * `stripComments`. Quotes and backticks are kept so the token stream still
 * parses by eye; only what is between them is erased.
 *
 * `${…}` interpolations inside a template literal are KEPT, because they are
 * executable code, not string content. Erasing them would hide exactly the
 * detail some tripwires exist to check — a rate-limit bucket keyed on
 * `` `x:${user.id}` `` versus one keyed on `` `x:${clientIp}` `` is the
 * difference between limiting an account and limiting a forgeable header, and
 * both collapse to the same blank if the interpolation goes with the text.
 *
 * WHY BOTH ARE NEEDED. `stripComments` deliberately preserves literals (there is
 * a test asserting exactly that), because plenty of tripwires need to read a
 * literal — "is MAIL_HOST still `mail.nxeon.cloud`?". But a tripwire asserting a
 * CALL is present must not match a mention of that call inside a string, and
 * this repo is full of such mentions: error copy, audit-log `action` values, and
 * doc strings that quote the very function being checked. Comments alone are not
 * enough here — `"Couldn't apply forwarding on the mail server"` and
 * `detail: "mailbox.suspend"` are executable code, and a naive grep is happy
 * with either.

## Summary

Built Phase 2 of the multi-registrar plan (Namecheap-only, per the scope change — eNom has no API) in an isolated worktree: `/opt/nxeon-wip-namecheap`, branch `feature/namecheap-registrar`. Nothing was committed (not asked to); nothing in `/opt/nxeon` was touched except one accidental, immediately-reverted action (see below).

### Files created
- `lib/registrars/types.ts` — `RegistrarClient` interface, matched field-for-field against `lib/registrar.ts`'s Phase-1-consolidated exports.
- `lib/registrars/namecheap.ts` — real Namecheap XML client (567 lines).
- `lib/registrars/index.ts` — `ALL_REGISTRARS`, `configuredRegistrars()`, `registrarById()`.
- `test/registrar-merge-cheapest.test.ts`, `test/registrar-renewal-freeze.test.ts`, `test/registrar-namecheap-xml.test.ts` (19 new tests, all passing).

### Files modified
`lib/registrar.ts` (exported `disableRegistrarAutorenew`), `lib/settings.ts` (`registrar_namecom_enabled`="true", `registrar_namecheap_enabled`="false"), `lib/tools/domain-availability.ts` (rewritten as a per-registrar fan-out with cheapest-merge), `lib/stripe.ts`, `lib/actions-domains.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts`, `worker/billing.ts`, `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx`, `components/customer/DomainSearch.tsx`, `components/customer/DomainRegisterWizard.tsx`, `prisma/schema.prisma`.

### Namecheap endpoints used (verified via Google's cache of namecheap.com/support/api — the live pages 403'd my fetcher — cross-checked against Namecheap's own Go/PHP SDKs and PyNamecheap)
`domains.check`, `users.getPricing` (domains.check carries NO price for ordinary names — only premium — a real gotcha), `domains.create`, `domains.renew`, `domains.getInfo`, `domains.dns.setCustom`, `domains.setRegistrarLock`/`getRegistrarLock`, `domains.dns.getHosts`/`setHosts` (replace-all, no per-record CRUD), `domains.transfer.create`/`getList`. Base URLs: `api.namecheap.com` / `api.sandbox.namecheap.com`, both `/xml.response`, gated sandbox-safe-by-default like `lib/paypal.ts`.

**Confirmed real API gaps** (documented in code, not guessed around): no endpoint to fetch an EPP/auth code (dashboard-only), no endpoint to cancel an inbound transfer, no endpoint to toggle a domain's own auto-renew.

### Still needed before this can go live
1. **`NAMECHEAP_API_USER` and `NAMECHEAP_USERNAME`** — still blank in `.env`; need the real values from the owner.
2. **IP whitelisting** — `51.79.162.96` must be added manually in the Namecheap dashboard (Profile → Tools → Business & Dev Tools → API Access → Whitelisted IPs). No API exists to do this remotely. Every real call fails until both are done.
3. `registrar_namecheap_enabled` ships **off** by default, per the plan's staged rollout.

### Renewal-price finding
Both name.com's client and the availability fan-out **already had** `renewCents` end-to-end — it just wasn't displayed everywhere, and worse, `renewDomainAction`/`domainAutoRenewSweep`/the domain detail page were all **charging off the original registration price** at renewal time, not a true renewal rate. Fixed by adding `Domain.renewPriceCents`/`renewCostCents` (+ same on `DomainOrderIntent`) and wiring registration/transfer to freeze them, renewal paths to read them. Added the "renews at $X/yr" copy to `DomainSearch.tsx` result rows and the wizard's Review step/Order Summary (previously only shown in the wizard's first step).

### One incident, self-corrected
`npx prisma generate` writes into the **shared** `node_modules` (symlinked from `/opt/nxeon`) — the first run clobbered the live app's Prisma Client with types for columns that don't exist in the real DB yet. Caught it, reverted `schema.prisma` to HEAD, regenerated to restore the shared client to match production exactly, then re-applied the schema edits by hand without regenerating again. The two new nullable columns exist only in this worktree's `schema.prisma` text — application code reads/writes them via explicit `as any` casts (commented inline) until someone runs `npx prisma db push && npx prisma generate` for real as part of promoting this branch. `node_modules` is a symlink that git does **not** treat as ignored despite `node_modules/` being in `.gitignore` (confirmed) — whoever commits this branch should stage files explicitly, not `git add -A`.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm test`: 1244 tests, 1210 pass, exactly the same 34 pre-existing failures as baseline (diffed line-for-line — identical set). `registrar-leak-guard.test.ts` and `registrar-error.test.ts` pass unchanged.
